claim_verdicts.evidence: labels.md:104-105: "Unlike names and UIDs, labels do not provide uniqueness. In general, we expect many objects to carry the same label(s)." names.md:12-15: "a Name that is unique for that type of resource" ... "you can only have one Pod named myapp-1234 within the same namespace". Round 2 lesson text (sec 4 "A Pod's name is unique among the Pods of its namespace; a label is not.", sec 6 misconception 1, quiz q1 b "Pod names must be unique in a namespace") now scoped to Pods, matching the docs.

labels.md (LIST and WATCH filtering, line 202+): label selectors filter the sets of objects returned by list operations. kubectl v1.34.3 get --help: "-l, --selector='': Selector (label query) to filter on". Captured stage-2 output: -l app=web lists web-stable, web-test only. Sec 4 "A Pod named web-proxy with app: proxy would still be left out" follows: equality on the app label, name not read.

labels.md:111-113: "all must be satisfied so the comma separator acts as a logical AND (&&) operator." kubectl v1.34.3 get --help for -l: "Matching objects must satisfy all of the specified label constraints." Captured output: -l app=web,track=stable returns web-stable only.

labels.md:12-15: labels are "meaningful and relevant to users, but do not directly imply semantics to the core system. Labels can be used to organize and to select subsets of objects." Unchanged since round 1.

kubectl v1.34.3 get --help: "--show-labels=false: When printing, show all labels as the last column". Executed `kubectl get pods -n donhang --show-labels` (read-only, server v1.34.11): header ends with LABELS, values like `app=api,pod-template-hash=746f868bc9`.

git show stage-2:deploy/k8s/lessons/labelled-pods.yaml: three Pods in donhang, all caddy:2.10.0; web-stable app: web/track: stable (7-11), web-test app: web/track: test (20-24), proxy app: proxy/track: stable (33-37). Lesson block lines=1-15 matches verbatim.

git show stage-2:scripts/k8s/labels.sh: line 6 defines show() as echo of "$ " plus the command, then runs it; 8 apply namespace.yaml; 9 delete --ignore-not-found; 11 apply; 12 wait Ready; 19-25 four lists; 27-28 comment + delete. Lesson block lines=8-25 is verbatim. web-replicaset.yaml and web-deployment.yaml@stage-2 both have selector matchLabels app: web, supporting "objects of the next lessons, which also select app=web". Output block diff vs labels.txt: empty.

Executed kubectl v1.34.3 (read-only): `kubectl get pods -n donhang -l app=web` printed `No resources found in donhang namespace.`; `kubectl get pods -n kube-node-lease` (namespace with no Pods, no selector) printed `No resources found in kube-node-lease namespace.`, exit 0 — same message form as the sec 7 emptiness check. Not run unfiltered on donhang as empty: it currently holds the real deploy.

labels.md: labels "do not directly imply semantics to the core system". No object in the lesson selects on track; sec 6 misconception 3 symptom ("-l track=stable lists proxy, whose name has no stable in it") matches the captured output (proxy, web-stable). Docs opened this round: labels.md, names.md (refs mirror), kubectl v1.34.3 get --help.

issues.text: The new emptiness check tells me what I should see, but not what to do if `kubectl get pods -n donhang` lists other Pods (e.g. leftovers from an earlier exercise). I would not know whether to delete them, ignore them, or expect step 1's output to differ.
issues.quote: Run this while `donhang` holds nothing else, as at this point of the track: `kubectl get pods -n donhang` should print `No resources found in donhang namespace.`
issues.fix: Append one clause: "; if it lists other Pods, step 1's `LABELS` and `-l track=stable` lists will include them too." (or say which command removes them).
